docs.title: Copernicus Painter
docs.text: Texture painting inside Houdini, the way Substance 3D Painter works. You stack layers of materials, decide where each shows with masks, change them with filters and paint with brushes. It's all built on Copernicus, Houdini's GPU image network, so nothing leaves Houdini and everything stays procedural.

docs.title: What's in it
docs.text:
• Layers of procedural materials and texture sets, with opacity and blend modes per layer and per channel (BaseColor, Roughness, Metalness, Normal, Height, AO...).
  • Masks that say where a layer shows: paint them, fill them, pick UV islands, or use generators that read the baked mesh maps (Dirt, Edge Wear, Curvature, Ambient Occlusion...). Grunges and procedural noises work as masks too.
  • Filters:
    • mask filters (Blur, Levels, Histogram Scan, Warp...) on the mask stack;
    • layer filters (HSL, Color Balance, Gradient Map, Height to Normal...) on a layer's channels.
  • Brushes and alphas: brush presets, stamps, a library of alpha shapes; paint in 3D or in the 2D (UV) view.
  • A 2D view next to the 3D one: the model laid out flat by its UVs, painted at the same time.
  • Your own smart materials and smart masks, made in Copernicus and saved to your library.
  • UDIMs, texture set groups, baking, and export presets for engines and renderers.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
1. Installation

  3. Layers, masks and filters

The guided tour

Help on the Painter shelf has two guided tours: one walks you through a first project step by step, highlighting each part of the screen as it goes; the other covers making your own smart material. Help also opens this documentation. The first tour starts by itself the first time you open the Painter desktop.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Houdini 22.0 (tested on 22.0.459). Houdini 21 is not supported.
  • Windows 10 or 11.
  • The tool's assets were saved in Houdini Indie. A full commercial Houdini asks to switch the session to Limited Commercial when it loads them; Indie and Apprentice don't ask.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
1. Close Houdini.
  2. Unzip CopernicusPainter_v<version>.zip into your Houdini preferences folder, next to the packages folder (not inside it): C:\Users\<you>\Documents\houdini22.0\CopernicusPainter\
  3. Copy CopernicusPainter\CopernicusPainter.json into that preferences folder's packages folder (create it if it isn't there): C:\Users\<you>\Documents\houdini22.0\packages\CopernicusPainter.json
  4. Start Houdini.

To update, delete the old CopernicusPainter folder first, then do the steps above.

docs.title: First launch
docs.text:
Pick the CopernicusPainter desktop from Houdini's desktop menu (top of the window). It lays Houdini out like a painting app:

  • the viewer, split into the 3D view and the 2D (UV) view;
  • Layers and Properties on the right;
  • the shelf of materials, brushes, masks and filters at the bottom;
  • the Painter shelf at the top left.

Button What it does Project Create a project from a mesh, or resume one Bake Bake the mesh maps (curvature, occlusion, position...) 2D View Split the viewer into 3D and 2D, or put the 2D view back on its framing Export Write the textures Library Make your own smart materials and smart masks Settings Your library folders Help The guided tours, and this documentation

The first time, the guided tour starts by itself. Close it with End tour; it is under Help whenever you want it back. Then go on with your first project.

docs.title: The layer stack
docs.text:
Layers stack like in Substance Painter: the top layer covers the ones below. Each row has:

  • the arrow, which shows the layer's masks and filters;
  • the eye, to hide it;
  • its icon and name (double-click to rename);
  • Opacity and the blend mode (Normal, Add, Subtract, Multiply, Screen, Overlay);
  • delete (the red cross).

Drag rows to reorder them. Right-click a layer for Duplicate Layer and Add Mask.

At the top of the panel:

  • Groups: the texture sets of the project. Each has its own stack; the eye hides it in the viewer.
  • Channel: which channel the viewer shows (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal...).
  • Resolution: the project's texture size.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Click a layer, a mask or a filter: its controls show in Properties.

For a layer:

  • Fill: how it's put on the model.
    • Projection: UV, or Planar, Triplanar, Cylinder, Spherical with a gizmo in the viewer (Edit Gizmo). Clip to shape limits it to the gizmo.
    • Tiling, Offset and Rotation. The lock keeps U and V together.
  • Material: which channels the layer writes (click to turn one off) and their values.
  • The material's own controls: colours, patterns, wear, grain... whatever its maker put on it.

docs.title: Masks
docs.text:
A mask says where its layer shows: white shows the layer, black hides it. Masks stack like layers. The first starts from black, each one goes on top with its own blend mode and opacity, and inv inverts one. Several masks add up the way their blend modes say.

Ways to add a mask:

  • From the shelf: drag a Generator, a Grunge or a Procedural onto a layer.
  • Right-click the layer > Add Mask:
    • Paint Mask: paint it (Painting).
    • Fill (White), Fill (Black): the whole layer, or none of it, to paint into.
    • Procedural Generators > Smart Mask / Grunge: then pick one in Properties.
    • Mesh Fill: whole UV islands or connected pieces; Select Islands in Properties, click them in the viewer (3D or 2D), Enter when done.

docs.title: Generators
docs.text: Generators make masks from the baked maps, like Substance Painter's: Dirt, Edge Wear, Curvature, Ambient Occlusion, Cavity, Thickness, Light, Position Gradient, 3D Linear Gradient, World Space Normals, UV Border Distance, Mask Builder and more. They need the bake (see Bake). Each has its controls in Properties: amount, contrast, a grunge to break it up...

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
Filters change what is below them. There are two kinds, on the Filters shelf:

  • Mask filters (Filters > Mask): Blur, Directional Blur, Levels, Histogram Scan, Histogram Shift, Clamp, Invert, Contrast / Luminosity, Highpass, Sharpen, Warp, Slope Blur, Transform, Bevel, Mask Outline. Dropped on a layer, a mask filter goes on its mask stack and works on the masks below it.
  • Layer filters (Filters > Layer): HSL, Color Correct, Color Balance, Gradient Map, Contrast / Luminosity, Invert, Levels, Blur, Sharpen, Height to Normal. They work on the layer's channels (its colour, roughness, height...).

Dropped on a layer, a layer filter shows under its masks as a fx row with on/off, opacity and delete. Several filters run in order, each on the result of the one before. Click the row for its controls.

docs.title: Undo
docs.text: Every change here (a layer added, a mask's blend mode, a slider let go, a filter deleted) is one undo step.

docs.title: The shelf and your libraries
docs.text: The shelf at the bottom of the Painter desktop shows your libraries, like Substance Painter's shelves. It shows the samples that come with the tool, plus any library folders you add.

docs.title: The shelf tabs
docs.text:
Tab What is in it How you use it Materials Procedural materials with controls (Skin, Fabric, Leather, Metal, Wood, Stone, Concrete, Plastic) Drag onto Layers: a new layer Textures Image texture sets (BaseColor, Roughness, Normal... files) Drag onto Layers Smart Masks Your saved masks Drag onto a layer: a mask Brushes Brush presets Click: paint with it; or drag onto a layer Alphas Brush tips (greyscale images) Click: the brush tip Procedurals Noises and patterns, one mask each Drag onto a layer: a mask Grunges Wear and dirt maps Drag onto a layer: a mask Generators Masks from the baked maps (Dirt, Edge Wear...) Drag onto a layer: a mask Filters Mask filters and layer filters Drag onto a layer
  • Groups are folders: click one to go in, < Back to go out.
  • Search looks in every library and every group.
  • The buttons on the right switch the icon size and refresh the shelf after you add files on disk.

docs.title: Your own library
docs.text:
Settings on the Painter shelf lists your library folders.

  • Add... picks a folder. A new, empty folder gets the category folders made for you.
  • Remove takes one off the list (nothing is deleted), and Open shows it in Explorer.
  • Show the samples turns the samples (read-only) on or off.
  • Save Settings keeps it.

A library folder has one folder per tab:

MyLibrary/
├── materials/        procedural materials: a folder X with X.cpio (+ X.jpg icon)
├── textures/         texture sets: a folder of images (+ shader.jpg icon)
├── smart_masks/      X.cpio
├── brushes/          X.json brush presets (+ X.png)
├── alphas/           greyscale images
├── procedurals/      X.cpio
├── grunges/          X.cpio, or an image
├── generators/       X.cpio
└── filters/          X.cpio

Inside each, any folder that isn't an item is a group, at any depth (materials/Metal/Rust/...). The thumbnail sits next to the item: <name>.jpg or .png, shader.jpg for a texture set, and an alpha is its own.

Texture sets are read by their file names: basecolor/albedo/diffuse, roughness, metal, normal, height/displacement, ao/occlusion, opacity... A folder of textures downloaded from Poly Haven or similar works as it is.

Materials and masks you make yourself are saved here by the Library window: see Making smart materials.

docs.title: Making smart materials
docs.text:
A smart material is a Copernicus subnet:

  • inside, any COP network: noises, patterns, ramps, filters;
  • outputs named after the channels it makes (BaseColor, Roughness, Metalness, Normal, Height...);
  • inputs named after the baked maps it reads (Curvature, Occlusion, Position...);
  • controls on the subnet, which show in Properties when its layer is selected.

A smart mask is the same with one output, Mask. Both are made in the Library window and saved to your library. Help > Make your own smart material is a step-by-step tour of it.

docs.title: 1. Open the Library window
docs.text:
Click Library on the Painter shelf.

At the top, pick Smart Material or Smart Mask.

docs.title: 2. New
docs.text:
• Name it.
  • Pick its Channels (outputs): BaseColor, Roughness, Metalness, Normal, Height, Specular, AO, Opacity.
  • Pick the Baked maps it reads (inputs): normal, worldnormal, position, occlusion, curvature, edge, cavity, thickness, height, alpha.
  • Click Create and edit.

You get a layer with a ready subnet: every output is there, typed and named, fed by a constant, and every input is wired to its bake. The network editor opens inside it.

A smart mask goes on the selected layer instead (Create on selected layer).

Already built a subnet yourself? Select it in the network editor and click Use selected subnet.

docs.title: 3. Build inside
docs.text: Replace the constants with your network. The layer updates while you work, so you see the material on the model as you build it.

docs.title: 4. Controls
docs.text:
Add the parameters you want to change later to the subnet itself: right-click it > Edit Parameter Interface. Use them inside with ch("../name").

They show in Properties when the layer is selected:

  • sliders, toggles and menus;
  • colours, as colour fields;
  • ramps, with their point editor;
  • folders, as collapsible sections.

docs.title: 5. Check and save
docs.text:
Editing shows what the Painter makes of your subnet, so fix anything it marks before saving:

  • which output feeds which channel;
  • which input gets which bake;
  • warnings, such as a bake not done yet or a name it doesn't know.

Then fill in:

  • Save as: its name on the shelf.
  • Library: one of your library folders (Settings); the samples are read-only.
  • Group: optional, e.g. Metal/Rust.

Click Save to Library. It is saved with a rendered icon, and appears on the Materials shelf (smart masks on Smart Masks).

From library > Edit opens a saved one again as a new layer (for a mask, Add to selected layer).

docs.title: Names the Painter reads
docs.text:
Output Channel Type BaseColor Base colour RGB Roughness Roughness Mono Metalness Metalness Mono Normal Normal (tangent space, 0-1) RGB Height Height Mono Specular, AO, Opacity Specular, ambient occlusion, opacity Mono Mask the mask (smart masks only) Mono Input Baked map Normal, WorldNormal, Position Normals (tangent / world) and position (RGB) Occlusion, Curvature, Edge, Cavity, Thickness, Height, Alpha Mono maps

Names are CamelCase and matched ignoring case. A smart mask with an input named Mask is a mask filter: it gets the masks below it.

Normal strength

Copernicus' Height to Normal strength works per UV unit, so a fine pattern gets very strong normals quickly. The samples are set so their normal map is about 95% flat on average. If a material looks all bumps, lower its normal strength.

docs.title: Painting
docs.text: You paint masks: where a layer shows. Paint white to show the layer, erase or paint black to hide it. The stroke lands on the model in the 3D view and on its flat copy in the 2D view at the same time, so paint in whichever is easier.

docs.title: Pick a brush
docs.text:
Open Brushes on the shelf and click one. If the selected layer has no paint mask, one is added, and you are painting with that brush straight away. You can also drag a brush onto any layer.

Group Brushes Basic Hard, Soft, Airbrush, Pencil, Marker, Eraser, Soft Eraser, Smooth, Smudge Texture Chalk, Bristle, Spray, Splatter, Sponge, Grunge, Rust, Scratches, Dirt, Cloud Stamps Rivet, Bolt, Screw, Stitches, Bullet Hole, Cracks, Drops

The brush is one for the whole project, as in Substance Painter. Change it, and every paint mask paints with it.

Alphas on the shelf are brush tips: click one and the brush paints with it. There are 32 in four groups (Shapes, Brush Tips, Grunge, Stamps); add your own greyscale images to your library's alphas folder.

docs.title: Brush settings
docs.text:
Select the paint mask: Properties shows the brush.

  • Brush: the stroke preview, the brush type (Paint, Erase, Smooth, Smudge, Texture, Stamp, Dirt, Cloud), Size, Flow, Softness and Spacing. Mirror paints on both sides of an axis.
  • Alpha: the brush tip. Click the slot to pick an image, drop one on it, or click one in the list below. Rotation and Scale turn and size it.
  • Fill: fill the whole mask black, white, or with a value.

docs.title: In the viewer
docs.text:
With the paint mask selected, the viewer is in the paint tool. Press Tab in the viewport if it isn't. Paint with the left mouse button; Houdini's paint keys work (for example F to change values, C for the brush operation, Shift+F1 for the hints).

Each stroke is an undo step.

Painting colour

You paint masks today, so a layer shows its material where you paint. To paint a colour, use a layer with that colour (a material with its colour set) and paint its mask.

docs.title: Your first project
docs.text: The whole loop: a project, the baked maps, a few layers, export. Each part has its own page for the details.

docs.title: 1. Create a project
docs.text:
A project is one node in /obj that holds the whole texture set: the layer stack, the masks, the bakes. Click Project on the Painter shelf (or New… at the top of the Layers panel).

Field What it is Project Name The name of the project node Geometry Source A Houdini node (its path, or Select) or a file (FBX, OBJ, BGEO) Split Geometry By How the mesh is cut into texture sets: by Groups, Name, Connectivity, or Don't Split Use UDIMs One texture per UV tile (1001, 1002...) Normal Map Y Direction OpenGL (+Y): Blender, Unity, Maya, Houdini. DirectX (-Y): Unreal, 3ds Max

The mesh needs UVs and normals. Click Initialize Project.

Each texture set (a group from the split) has its own layer stack. Pick it in Groups at the top of the Layers panel; the eye hides it in the viewer.

docs.title: Several projects in one hip
docs.text: A hip can hold several projects. Project at the very top of the Layers panel says which one you are on: click it to list them all and pick another. Opening a hip opens the project you used last in it.

docs.title: 2. The 3D and 2D views
docs.text:
The viewer is split. On the left is your model; on the right, the 2D view: the same model laid out flat by its UVs, like Substance Painter's 2D view. Everything shows in both, and you can paint in both.

In the 2D view you pan and zoom as in any Houdini view (hold Space and drag with the middle mouse to pan; the wheel zooms towards the pointer). It never rotates, and moving it is not an edit, so it adds nothing to undo. 2D View on the shelf puts it back on its home framing.

docs.title: 3. Bake the mesh maps
docs.text:
Click Bake. The baked maps are what generators and smart materials read: curvature for edge wear, occlusion for dirt in the cavities, position for gradients.

Pick the resolution, the low-poly mesh (your project's), optionally a high-poly and a cage, tick the maps and click Bake Textures. Bake at least Position and World Normal, which the projections need. Preview Baked Channel shows a map on the model.

docs.title: 4. Layers
docs.text:
The shelf at the bottom is your library. Drag a material onto the Layers panel. Materials are procedural, with controls; Textures are image sets. Drop more, then add masks and filters to them.

The GIF shows a red brick, then a tiger skin over it, a Dirt mask so the tiger only shows in the cavities, and an HSL filter on the tiger. All of that is on Layers, masks and filters.

docs.title: 5. Paint
docs.text: Click a brush on the Brushes shelf: the layer gets a paint mask and you are painting. See Painting.

docs.title: 6. Export
docs.text:
Click Export.

Setting What it is Template Which maps and how they are named and packed: PBR Metallic, Unreal Engine 5 (packed ORM), Unity URP/HDRP, Houdini / Mantra Output Directory Where the files go (Open Output Directory opens it) File Type PNG, JPEG, EXR or TIFF Resolution The exported size Merge groups by UDIM tile On UDIM projects: one file per tile with every texture set in it Export as Sequence Frames from Start to End, for animated layers

Export Textures writes them; Save Settings keeps the choice with the project.

docs.title: Undo
docs.text: Everything you do in the panels is one undo step: Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z, and the panels follow. Moving the views isn't an edit.
